places.name: McConkey's Ferry landing (Pennsylvania side)
places.src: Derived: Johnson Ferry House (NJ) at 40.2993,-74.8682 per OSM + river ~275 m wide (ABT: ~300 yd) + Washington Crossing Bridge ~40.2986,-74.872; NOT surveyed
places.note: Army embarked here from about 5-6 p.m. on 25 Dec 1776 (ATL; WP). Washington Crossing Historic Park (PA). River flows SE. Use as the departure point; snap to the real bank in the basemap.

places.name: Johnson's Ferry landing (New Jersey side)
places.src: Derived from OSM Johnson Ferry House 40.2993,-74.8682 (river bank ~350 m west); NOT surveyed
places.note: Landing on the NJ shore; guns over by ~3 a.m., march began ~4 a.m. 26 Dec (ATL; WP). Washington Crossing State Park.

places.name: Birmingham (road fork where the army split)

places.name: Hessian main posts (Rall + Lossberg quarters, north half of town)
places.src: Approx. from americanwars.org ch. VIII/WP order of battle: Rall and Lossberg regiments quartered in northern Trenton

places.name: Knyphausen regiment quarters (south, by the Assunpink bridge)

notes.orientation: Delaware flows SE from McConkey's Ferry (PA, west bank) to Trenton Falls; the NJ side is the EAST bank. Trenton: King Street (N. Warren St) and Queen Street (N. Broad St) run N-S from the Assunpink creek in the south up to the head of the streets at today's Battle Monument (north). The Assunpink flows W-E south of the town; the 'bridge' on Queen St is the key. Princeton lies NE of Trenton (~12 miles); the Post Road runs Trenton - Maidenhead (Lawrenceville) - Stony Brook - Princeton; the night march swung EAST (Sandtown - Quaker Bridge) then north.
notes.accuracy_warning: Anchors from OSM Nominatim in this session: Johnson Ferry House, Old Barracks, Battle Monument, N/S Broad and Warren Streets, Assunpink Dr, Mill Hill Park, Nassau Hall, Princeton Battlefield / Mercer Oak, Stony Brook Bridge, Quaker Road, Bear Tavern Rd, Scotch Rd, Pennington Rd, River Rd, Calhoun Street Bridge, Lawrenceville, Kingston, Bordentown, Burlington, Bristol, Morristown. Everything else (the river and creek lines, Birmingham, Five Mile Run, Stockton Hollow, Sandtown, Quaker Bridge, Frog Hollow, Thomas Clarke house, route legs) is INTERPOLATED or from memory, flagged by large acc_m. Overpass/NHD could not be reached; snap rivers/roads to NHD+OSM in the basemap and use Stryker (1898) and Fischer's endpaper maps for the 1776 street grid.
notes.flags: Continental Army: the Grand Union flag was the Continental flag in Dec 1776 (Stars and Stripes not adopted until 14 June 1777); regimental colours by unit. British: Union Flag of 1707-1800 (St George + St Andrew). Hessians: Hesse-Kassel regimental colours (Rall, Lossberg, Knyphausen regiments each had its own); no single national flag. Do NOT show Leutze's painting (it shows a flag not yet adopted).
notes.reservoirs_dams: Do not draw any modern lakes or bridges: Washington Crossing Bridge, the Delaware & Raritan Canal and Carnegie Lake (Princeton, 1906) are modern; the Delaware & Raritan Canal runs near the Princeton end and the Assunpink Creek is now partly culverted through Trenton.
notes.weather_for_map: Night of 25-26 Dec: nor'easter, sleet and snow (ATL; ABT). Night 2-3 Jan: temperature fell ~20 degF and the mud froze (PAW; WP). See FACT_NOTES_jersey.md J.
